title: The Alps
summary: Use these eighty-five nights as one winter life, not a circuit of famous names. The town is still open because the children's U12 program has to win first: recurring peers, almost-daily training, a walkable place, dependable snow and a quiet work room. Apex 2100 in Tignes is the leading live option after a very positive September 17 admissions call: Britt sounded like Allie and Charlie would be a U12 fit, and a January–March day-athlete winter is the intended path if the group does not fill. Ski video is confirmation, not a high bar. Silvaplana remains a strong Swiss read. Val d'Isère and Crans-Montana are still live. Stay inside ninety days, then hand off to Copenhagen on Saturday, April 1.

season.summary: This is a true high-Alpine winter: cold, snow-covered and short on daylight, which is the point of the stay if a race program is real.
notes: Val d'Isère January normals are about 31°F by day and 16°F overnight, with about three inches of precipitation, mostly as snow. Recheck 2028 conditions for the valley that actually wins.
The Engadin runs colder than the French high resorts; Crans-Montana is a little milder. None of that replaces a local avalanche bulletin.
March warms and the light returns, but snow reliability still has to be a reason the base was chosen, not an afterthought.
Pack serious winter clothing, ski gear and indoor backups for storm days. Do not treat a sunny brochure photo as the daily forecast.

base.recommendation: One apartment in a real town, booked only after the ski program is real
base.reason: The Alpine base has to win on Allie and Charlie's recurring U12 training, ordinary community life, dependable snow, a quiet work room and a stay inside ninety days. A famous name is useful only if it serves that daily life. Do not rent in Val d'Isère, Tignes, Crans-Montana or the Engadin until a program can actually take them.
requirements: A confirmed U12 race-team or equivalent peer-group placement before the housing deposit
A walkable town with groceries, a bus or lift, and minimal daily driving
At least two bedrooms plus a closed-door workspace, or three bedrooms
Verified fibre or high-quality fixed broadband and strong mobile backup
Heating, laundry, a full kitchen, ski storage and blackout curtains
Written confirmation that the desk and internet can support repeated video calls
Flexible cancellation until 2027–28 program packages are published

bookFirst: Submit the Apex OpenApply application and U12 ski videos once Britt sends the link
Use the late-November / early-December Apex virtual open house
Send ACM race history and current skiing video if Crans-Montana is still in play
Follow up Club des Sports de Val d'Isère, Ski Club Verbier and Ski Club de Bagnes if they have not replied
Reconnect with GR Ski Racing Team Silvaplana around July 2027 when 2027–28 packages are available
Book the winter apartment only after a program can take Allie and Charlie
Recheck 2028 lift calendars, school-holiday weeks and snow reports for the chosen valley
planningNotes: The calendar stay is eighty-five nights, and it must not exceed ninety days.
The Apex call was strongly positive. Video and OpenApply still have to happen, but Britt treated the kids as a likely U12 fit. Housing waits on a written offer.
If Tignes wins, budget about two and a half weeks off academy snow in February unless they join the optional Italy camp.
Ski Zenit and the Apex Les Crosets camps are backups, not a continuous U12 race-team placement.
Club des Sports de Tignes, PDS Racing and ESS Verbier are closed leads unless they produce a stronger club referral.
Allie's birthday is Tuesday, January 18; Brian's birthday is Sunday, March 12. Keep both inside ordinary family time, not travel days.
Copenhagen is the Saturday, April 1 handoff. Do not spend the last Alpine week adding a second valley.

programs.name: Apex 2100 Academy
programs.contactActivity: Admissions Zoom with Britt Tilston on September 17, 2026. Earlier: camps-to-academy handoff and scheduling emails.
programs.currentRead: Very positive admissions call. From the Ford Sayre / race-suit description, Britt treated Allie and Charlie as a likely U12 fit; ski video is the usual confirmation, not a high bar. January–March as day athletes on snow and afternoon S&C is the intended path if the group does not fill. Applications for 2027–28 are already open.
programs.nextStep: Submit the OpenApply application and ski videos once Britt sends the link; use the late-November virtual open house.
callNotes: Fit — After hearing Ford Sayre racing and Allie in a GS/SL suit, Britt said a technical base at U12 is generally a fit and not to worry about a slight backseat. The ability range at U12 is wide and still developing. Video is how they confirm.

Peers — U12 is the flexible group: cap 16, typically 10–16, about 12 this year. Younger groups stay small; the academy is larger higher up (about 24–28 U14s, 48 U16s, 80 FIS athletes). U12 boarders are mostly British families who live relatively nearby. Americans, Canadians and a Chilean family already use the same day-student model with parents in Tignes for the winter.

Language and school — English-language British-system academy. Most U12s join Apex classroom for the winter term, then return to a home school in April. Homeschoolers can sit in that classroom with other independent-education kids, or go home after lunch. Racing is the local French GS/SL series.

On snow — Five half-days a week, lifts at 9 a.m. Mondays mix free skiing, telemark and snowboard. Other days are mostly gates, with free-ski to the lift each lap. They race local French hills by team van; the furthest is about 1 hour 15 minutes to La Plagne. A racing license comes through the affiliated club.

Week shape — Monday afternoon ski; Tuesday full education plus strength and conditioning, sometimes cross-country or roller hockey. Wednesday–Friday: morning ski, lunch, school and S&C from 2:00–6:30 p.m. Saturday morning ski if there is no race; Sunday off. Homeschoolers can leave after lunch and come back for S&C. House parents are on duty for day students too.

February — The academy leaves Tignes after the first week for an optional Italy camp (across the Fréjus tunnel in recent winters), then a school break. Skip the camp and you have about two and a half weeks of free-skiing in a busy holiday period.

Town — Compact compared with a big valley like Whistler. Free shuttle every 15 minutes; groceries and restaurants in Tignes; bus to Val d'Isère about 30 minutes. A car is optional except for valley supermarket runs.

Money and timing — This winter a U12 day athlete is about €20,000 (10% below the ~€23,000 full package). 2027–28 fees come in January. A three-month stay can get an offer as early as March 2027. Shorter weekly-rate stays wait until summer, once full-term numbers are known.
